TRANSPARENCY IS PART OF THE FORECAST

Behind every signal,
a trail of evidence.

Two completed experiments. Real saved model outputs. Clearly stated limits.

01 / CLIMATE HISTORY

Learning from
45 years of weather.

Gradient boosting trained on ERA5 observations through 2016, selected on 2017–2020, and tested on 2021–2025. This is a retrospective climate experiment; it does not model real-time publication delays.

02 / ISSUED WARNINGS

What could we have
known beforehand?

150 dated GFS runs from 2026. One frozen forecast trajectory per warning. Early-summer error adjustment frozen before later-summer testing, with a conservative publication buffer.

THE EVENT DEFINITION

Three hot days.
Two different questions.

A hot day exceeds the location’s 90th percentile for that calendar date, using a fixed 1981–2010 reference.

DAY 1OnsetDAY 2ContinuesDAY 3+Ongoing

Onset labels confirm that the first hot day is followed by at least two more. Those future observations are used for verification only. This custom three-day definition is not the six-day WSDI index.

READ THE NUMBERS CORRECTLY

A probability is a signal,
not a promise.

Classification uses a cutoff selected before the test period. A 30% event probability may cross that study cutoff; it is not a public safety risk category.

  • F1 balances missed events and false alerts.
  • Recall is the fraction of observed events detected.
  • Precision is the fraction of alerts that were correct.
  • Observed means ERA5 verification, not a weather station.
WHAT THIS OBSERVATORY CANNOT CLAIM

Useful evidence.
Honest boundaries.

  • Seven representative grid locations do not cover all of Europe.
  • Historical replay uses an assumed publication buffer; historical delivery logs are unavailable.
  • Error adjustment can increase false alerts, particularly at seven days.
  • Live weather is experimental and has no future observed outcome.
  • The probability adjustment was developed for summer; outside May–September, live mode shows temperatures only.
